claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a slow pacing at the start.

citations.review_text: slow start, but immersive the longer you play and as your character evolves, would have no issues recommending to anyone, also good value for me, if your into short stories and gameplay, its probably not for you, if you like watching your characters grow and storylines evolve, its a must.

It's a great game, but it demands a huge time commitment and is very slow to get going. Personally, I found the combat and exploration frustrating and tedious. 

Writing is excellent, there's just too much of it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that camera controls and positioning can feel frustrating or get stuck in terrain.

citations.review_text: The overall graphics and gameplay, plus story mode are the highest they could be, we just did not like the camera controls and camera p;ayability.

So i'm only 15 hours in but..

Cons:
Controls ABSOLUTELY SUCK
The camera sucks, it gets stuck in terrain and you can't see well half the time
Character control sucks, they run into traps and it's damn near impossible to manipulate them individually.
inventory management sucks.
All the characters have the same british/irish accents, no veriety.
only a handful of companions to choose from, and you can only take 4 at a time severely limiting specialization.

Still going to give it a chance and play it through but BG2 was a MUCH better game for it's time.

I simply cannot belive the clunky, messy, buggy experience I'm having after giving it a chance for 16 hours. This cannot be the same game that went through so much development time, and has overwhelmingly positive reviews. I naturally came with high expectations, but still.

Controls are questionable, with default either having to hold middle mouse button or right controller stick down to see interactable objects or rotate camera? Without an option to have it toggle the features?

I found controller to be the least worse choice, until I had to revert to keyboard and mouse as objects' description constantly appears over context menu, making it impossible to choose what to do with an item. There's so many UI issues overall.

No free camera, cannot look up? I feel trapped.

Coming from recent playthrough of Witcher 1, 2 and 3, with endless voice acting, it's so weird the main protagonist not voicing. Fine I guess, but why then choose to show the protagonist as a complete awkward mute in every conversation? It _breaks_ immersion, doesn't build it.

Bring science fiction through a space ship and world travel into the fantasy world as soon as the intro starts? I can enjoy science fiction, but don't mix it into fantasy worlds. Personal preference I guess, and I hope not to see any spaceship again in the playthrough, after the convenience crash.

I have more issues, also with the character designs and how they behave as a whole so far. I'm sure as soon as I get more tuned to this version of a dnd world, and forgets how wonderfully crafted Witcher world setting and characters are, I'll enjoy it more... but there are way too many issues at play here for me to recommend this sluggish experience. I've loved many rpg experiences, from dnd pen and paper, and Baldur's Gate I being especially a fond memory, at release and enhanced edition. This, so far, isn't a long game because it's good, but rather how the experience is crafted with controls, camera and UI. It doesn't help that i…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the learning curve as difficult or confusing for newcomers, requiring guides or time to understand systems.

citations.review_text: I have played a lot of turn based games since years ago, as well as DDO games. But Many people claim this is awesome. But there is absolutely no way this game isn't heavily robboted. Because there is a lot, a lot going wrong with this game. The gameplay sucks, the turn based combat is too tight to be enjoyable. Like you can do too little every turn. The learning curve is moronic, or rather, non existant. It's way too easy to get one shottefd by a trap right at the start and get stuck trying to find a way. It's simply way too broken to enjoy and people are not acknowledging. Overall, the multiplayer is really broken. Could be better. I can see how in time I will like this game. I only wish it wasn't 1 so broken, and 2, didn't take so long to be bearable.
Amazing story; use external guides to get a sense of how to make it the most fun.
For a player that has never played D&D, this game is amazing. It was kinda rough/overwhelming getting into, but once you get the hang of it, you'll love it!

its really fun but very confusing 
when i started the game i actually had no idea what i was doing i had to look up a guide
7 hours into a playthrough, i still dont know what im really doing
astarion is cool

claims.claim: Reviewers report technical issues involving crashes during gameplay or multiplayer sessions.

citations.review_text: it just crashed  ffs  and you cant kill some characters as role playing goes its very limited

I went into this game completely blind.  I saw the 4 tags.  I watched the gameplay videos.  I felt it was misleading since the tags did not include Turn-Based.  The videos were also cut in a way that did not show it was turn-based.  They looked closer to how Diablo IV gameplay was.  I would not have bought this game had it been upfront with how the gameplay is since I am not a fan of turn-based games.  Also, the click to move was not as responsive as Diablo's click to move.  I also had trouble playing with my friend when we had initially started, before I found out it was turn-based.  The game he kept trying to start would crash.  I would try to start one and the game would also crash for me.  We would have to start again and then have to go through creating our characters again.  It took almost an hour to actually get to play.  Just disappointed that the game was mispresented in the video clips.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the multiplayer mode is really bad because joining a server requires downloading, deselecting, downgrading, or updating mods manually and sometimes the download freezes.

citation.review_text:
The game is really bad when it comes to multiplayer mode. I have tried at least 50 times to join a server and each time i have to download new mods, deselect active mods, downgrade modes, update mods. Why these are not made automatically? When downloading mods sometimes the download freeze. When you finally find a server where you have everything, it's already gone. 

Please create an autojoin feature.

single_points.text: One reviewer reports running into a game-breaking bug where an early character named Gale has a persisting aura that hurts allies and soft locks progress.

citation.review_text:
First Baldurs gate game that ive actually ever paid attention or understood things for (yknow young kid just doing things on games)
Thought yknow what im all about these RPG style games and it looks brilliant, Holy crap the "Normal" or second from easiest setting is HARSH as a new player, i step the difficulty down a notch, still a nice bit of challenge but some times a bit too harsh.
Then just as you get passed 2 or 3 hours of play a pretty much game breaking bug where GALE a character encountered early on has a persisting aura that HURTS your allies. because you CANNOT move them away properly when reviving others and he is the last person alive you cannoy progress , you go to camp? cant long rest as its not registering him as alive or something stupid! apparantly a very very well known bug and has now 4 hours into it essentially soft locked me from ANY progress.it wouldnt be so bad if the game wasnt so extremely long winded and slow to play which was the whole appeal of it in the first place but for something like this to be going on frankly is not acceptable. the community forums just say the same fix that is not applicable in this sense and it feels and seems to be that the devs have completely abandoned this bug or even bothering to try and fix it.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-game players discover vast content and varied paths, though initial mechanics remain demanding.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a large amount of content and high replayability, with different choices leading to varied playthroughs and paths.

citations.review_text: there is soooooo much content and a supportive community online.

Over 300 hours on PS5 and almost another 100 here, this game is hands down the best RPG I've ever played, maybe even the best game period. I have probably 5 different playthroughs at this point, each of them offers something different every time. I constantly find new secrets and things to do, and it's really easy to just get lost in the world of it. This is the gold standard for RPGs as far as I'm concerned. I don't know if there will ever be another like it.
your choices provide so many variables its like having many games in one.

Infinitely replayable and countless branches of every storyline -- I can't believe I'm playing this three years after launch, even though I tried it on PS5 in 2023. 

The turn-based combat takes a lot of time to get used to, and it may make some players wary of playing it (Some of my friends don't enjoy turned-based combat), but if you avoid it for that reason, you'll be missing out on one of the best games to have released with infinite replayability, one of the most complicated-yet-addictive stories I've ever faced in a video game. 

As of now, I've spent 24 hours, and that's more than what many games last for one playthrough. In this one, I'm not even out of Act I yet, and it's not really the number of hours that's important, it's the fact that I can't tell how those hours have passed. Between figuring out turn-based combats, having to think twice about choosing a dialog option for fear of alienating friends, and discovering completely new areas with both senses of awe and fear, I can't tell where time went. 

I highly recommend it if you really love complex stories where your choice matters, which you can come back to over and over again, and which requires quite a bit of thinking to plan ahead (both in terms of progressing through the story and laying out combat tactics), this is the best game in this genre. 

Gemini said it best: There really is no other game that has quite the same mix as Baldur's Gate 3, even if there are others that rely on the same D&D e5 formula. 

Highly, highly recommended.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the opening hours and mechanics can feel overwhelming or difficult to learn for players unfamiliar with Dungeons and Dragons rules.

citations.review_text: WOW... what a game. So overwhelming to get into but very rewarding. Leaves you with that empty and depressed feeling after you complete it.

As a casual gamer I am very picky about the games I purchase. I do not like to throw money away needlessly and waited quite some time for a sale before grabbing BG3. Glad I did, but it's a lot to learn.
I played table top D&D when Gygax first created it, but aside from Dragons of Krynn, Pool of Radiance, and a few other early (1995-1999) D&D-based titles haven't touched it since the late 1990's. Setting up options/keystrokes took a few hours going back and forth between changes, short play, and more changes until I had things how I like them. Probably not an issue for a regular Larian or D&D player though.

D&D-style play isn't for everyone, but the game mechanics are handled well and are smooth. I had a rough go for the first 10 hours or so, having to learn and relearn spells, effects, choice outcomes, and generally understanding what causes what. Note that I'm still getting surprises after over 70 hours but they are becoming less frequent. I save frequently, replaying scenarios as I go...sometimes because I made a bad choice; sometimes just to see what else could go on. 

My gripes come from two places:
Learning curve if you don't have a current familiarity with D&D, spell actions, consequences, etc. then play will be frustrating? until you get up to speed.
 
I haven't found an 'UNDO' for a bad (wrong) keystroke other than backing out of a spell with ESC to choose a different action. It's pretty easy to accidentally trigger a wrong keypress on my keyboard and the only correction is to reload. MY bad but it would be nice to have an out.

I'm still in Act 1 and will stay there until I hit at least level 6 (level 7 if I can) before crossing into Act 2. I'm also trying diligently to avoid spoilers and guides although I do have to admit to a few. Buttons are easy to spot in scenes, levers not so much. You'll need to be able to see well, both from your character and your monitor. Managing the camera is an art form.

I'm playing with a C6 tandem 48" OLED, Z69…

[h1]Good, just not for me.[/h1]

This will be a negative review but in all fairness the game does deserve a thumbs up.

I tried twice to get into this game in a span of two years. Both times I ended up feeling unattracted to the story. Only the second time was I able to put my finger on exactly what it was.

First, it's the whole D&D thing. I'll start by saying that D&D is not by any stretch a bad game. But if you haven't played it, you WILL find it overwhelming. It requires a lot of time and patience to get to grips with all the mechanics. My problem is that BG3 doesn't do a very good job at delivering it to you piecemeal. From level 1 you are thrown knee-deep into the mechanics of D&D with no safety rails. The result? Combat feels unbalanced in favor of the AI. I think for those of us who have never played D&D, but who wanted to get into the game nonetheless, a beginner-friendly version of each class could've been added, with reduced spells and abilities or a simplified set of rules, just enough to get to grips with the core, and then be given full access to everything later on.

Secondly, it's the characters. They really do feel like caricatures of RPG tropes. Like they have distilled the essence of each stereotypical RPG character, injected it with hormones and steroids, and moulded them into characters that end up feeling unlikeable, tiresome and unidimensional. I just wanted them to shut the hell up and let me play, because I already knew what they would say or how they would act. They are predictable. Furthermore, each one comes packed with their own problem. This would've been cool and interesting were it not for the fact that their problems seem to compete with the main quest in urgency and importance. I stopped playing when I no longer could tell whether the game wanted me to get rid of the worm, or the vampire, or the magic eater, or the guy who explodes. I ended up thinking, damn, give me a break. You have crafted a wonderful world and I cannot slow down…

This game is a masterpiece. With zero experience in dice roll games or D&D, at first I can say that I found the game weird, starting from the movement and camera controls, to the turn based combat, it was just weird and I thought oh what a boring game I do not think I will like it, but as I spent a few more hours getting familiar with the systems and the stats I started to gain interest. And then, the game, the story, the details, the abilities, the interacions, the companions everything came together and since the day I started playing I just cannot put it down. It is simply the best game I have ever played in my life. Give it some hours, learn to play it and you will start a lovely, beautiful, thrilling game, the best gaming experience ever. Thanks Larian for creating this masterpiece. I am sure I will spend countless hours exploring everything. When you piece everything together and start a fight you will find everything mind blowing really. Can't explain in words what this game makes you experience. Loveeeeeeeeee it.

cohorts.summary: Long-term players praise the extensive character options and deep combat mechanics.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game offers extensive character creation options, multiple classes, and deep combat mechanics.

citations.review_text:
One of the 10 Best Games of All Time

I want to start off by saying that Baldur's Gate 3 is easily in my top 10 games of all time. I honestly don't think I'll see many games that come close to being as good, polished, and complete as this one. From start to finish, this game is an absolute masterpiece.

Let's start at the beginning.

A friend of mine kept trying to convince me to buy this game, but I was very hesitant. RPGs like this aren't usually my kind of thing, and I wasn't sure if I'd get into it. Eventually, though, he mentioned that it had hardcore, and that was enough to convince me to give it a shot.

I loaded it up, and wow. Just WOW.

From the music to the character customisation, the sheer number of classes, and the feeling of starting a brand-new adventure, I was hooked. There's something about this game that feels like sitting down with a very fine whisky and savouring every single sip. You don't want to rush it. You want to take your time, appreciate everything it has to offer, and enjoy every second of the experience.

And that's exactly what I did.

The story is fantastic, and the way your choices genuinely matter is something I absolutely love. Your decisions can have real consequences, and the game constantly reminds you that you're shaping your own adventure. It's crazy how much freedom you're given, and it makes every playthrough feel personal.

Then there's the loot. Oh boy, the loot. I absolutely love being a loot hobo, searching every container, checking every corner, and seeing what goodies I can get my hands on. And in a game this vast, there's always something else to discover.

That's what makes Baldur's Gate 3 so special to me. The world is enormous, the possibilities are ridiculous, and you can approach situations in so many different ways. You can play how you want, make your own decisions, experiment with different builds, and see where the adventure takes you. It gives you a level of freedom that I feel is becoming increasingly rare…

Baldurs Gate 3 is one of the most immersive RPGs I've played, I've spent hundreds of hours on this game in the past couple years. This game has great graphics, and an immersive environment, which really gets me into the setting. The combat mechanics are very in-depth, and it requires real strategy to defeat the enemies, the bosses are a real challenge on the higher difficulties. The character interactions and story paths are immense, and you'll never have a playthrough exactly the same. The only real issue with it for me was the performance, it is fine in the first zones, but the last areas take a real beefy computer to run well!

single_points.text: One reviewer says there is some camera control going in and out of indoor areas and some movement feels janky.

citation.review_text:
Baldur's Gate 3 was a genuine masterclass by Larian Studios. As a turn-based strategy/MMO game, there is a lot going for it, and a few things that don't - though many of these can be handled by the many thousands of mods available both ingame and through third party sources.

However, my current steam hours are non-reflective. I probably have closer to 1800 at the time of writing (My steam sometimes just.. does not track my game hours).

Immense replayability, immense room for discovery and fun if the style of game is one you enjoy or can grow into enjoying. A billion mods, anywhere from Withers' big natural breasts, to UI overhauls, to entirely new zones or game modes, or just adding in goofy weapons.

Billion times recommend based on that.

For the interest of fairness, there are a few control things that feel clunky. Some camera control going in/out of indoor areas. Some movement feels janky here and there. Attacking a target and in the nanosecond before you clicked they breathed and so you didn't click on them and hit the air instead.

I'd still recommend regardless.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the looting system is getting archaic and cumbersome and the dice roll gets super old very quickly.

citation.review_text:
Held off playing as long as I could to get max updates, and it was worth the wait... for the most part.

Liked:

1. Shadowheart...
2. Voice Acting, character design, and storytelling is top notch.
3. So much quest content.
4. Great in-game mod support, which I ended up with roughly 69 mods.

Disliked:

1. Looting system is getting archaic and cumbersome unless you enjoy picking up trash at every corner.
2. Stealing is pretty annoying when it comes to alerting the authorities. I got to a point where I just killed anyone who tried to arrest me.
3. The Dice Roll... gets super old very quickly.
4. I did not much care for Astorian.
5. I'm not a fan of the D&D math that figuring out an upgrade ended up just being how rare the gear was.

This is a very long game, so be prepared mentally and physically for a epic journey.
